title: AirQo Website API
subtitle: High-performance REST API backend for air quality data
description: A high-performance, scalable REST API backend for the AirQo website, providing access to air quality data, research publications, events, team information, and more. Built with Django REST Framework with a focus on performance, security, and developer experience.
problem: Air quality data across African cities needs to be accessible through a performant, well-documented API that supports complex filtering, pagination, and caching. The existing infrastructure needed modernization with proper API versioning, comprehensive documentation, and security hardening.
role: Built the V2 enhanced API endpoints with advanced features including comprehensive caching, query optimization, and improved error handling. Implemented the forum events API with complete nested response structures, universal slug-based lookups, and privacy-friendly URL patterns.
approach: Built on Django 5.1.4 with Django REST Framework 3.15.2. Uses PostgreSQL with connection pooling, multi-level caching strategy with 5-10 minute cache TTLs, smart pagination with cursor and page-based options, and OpenAPI 3.0 documentation via drf-spectacular. Implements privacy-friendly slug-based URLs instead of numeric IDs.
hardestDecision: Implementing the universal slug system across all models. This required careful migration planning to ensure backward compatibility with existing v1 endpoints while providing SEO-optimized, human-readable identifiers for all resources.
outcome: Powers the AirQo website (airqo.africa) serving air quality data across African communities. The API supports the website, mobile apps, and research integrations.
whatIdChange: Would implement GraphQL as an alternative to REST for more flexible querying, and add real-time WebSocket support for live air quality data streams.
